scope: Pinned files verified against captured Git tree; static whole-file review.

findings.detail: parseVMess converts numeric JSON port float64 to int before range checking, silently truncating fractional ports. String ports use Atoi and reject fractional values.

parseTrojan and parseHysteria2 apply QueryUnescape to User.Username already decoded by net/url. buildStreamSettings similarly applies QueryUnescape to values already decoded by ParseQuery (paths and spiderX). Literal plus and percent sequences can change a second time.
URL parsers discard ParseQuery errors, permitting partially parsed option maps. Invalid settings may silently disappear rather than generating a typed diagnostic.
parseSS discards the entire query before parsing, including plugin options. Conversion success therefore does not prove preservation of input semantics.

URL-based VLESS/Trojan/Hysteria parsers validate port and user credential but do not explicitly reject an empty Hostname. splitHostPort likewise accepts an empty host before a valid port. Downstream config loading may reject some such outputs; ConvertLink alone is not complete validation.

converter_test.go has three top-level tests: four fragment/load cases, four garbage inputs, and eight URL-host cases. Tests do not cover fractional ports, double decoding, empty hosts, or SS plugin preservation. No file/image deduplication is implemented here.
